summary: The Playwright tests are valid TypeScript and use Playwright API correctly. All locators and assertions are awaited and properly used. However, the selector strategy uses hard-coded data-test attributes which could be brittle. The navigation verification is too generic, only checking for '/product/' in the URL without confirming the exact product. Also, the test titles do not preserve the testCaseId and there is redundancy in asserting visibility of many similar product elements instead of a loop or more scalable approach.

issues.description: Selectors rely on hard-coded 'data-test' attributes enumerated explicitly from product-1 to product-26. This is brittle and not scalable.
issues.recommendation: Use a loop to verify product cards presence or a common class/data attribute to reduce code duplication.

issues.description: Test titles do not preserve the testCaseId (e.g., TC-001, TC-003) as requested in review rules.
issues.recommendation: Include testCaseId in the test titles for traceability.

issues.description: Navigation to product detail page test only verifies URL contains '/product/' but does not confirm the actual product ID in URL or on the page.
issues.recommendation: Enhance validation by asserting the specific product's detail page either by URL exact match or page content verification.

recommendations: Replace repeated locator assertions with a loop or helper function for scalability.
Improve navigation test assertions to ensure the correct product detail page is loaded.
Include testCaseId references in test titles to maintain traceability.
